questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L08_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

Which statement best matches a presentation purpose of explaining a proposal to school leaders?

answer.text: A. Study spaces are nice and school is a place.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and does not clearly explain the proposal.

answer.text: B. The school should provide a supervised study space after dismissal because many students remain on campus.

feedback.text: Correct. This states a clear proposal and reason for the intended audience.

answer.text: C. Everyone should agree with me because I said so.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not use respectful reasoning.

answer.text: D. My presentation is about several unrelated school topics.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This lacks a clear focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L08_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.02

Which slide choice best supports audience understanding?

answer.text: A. A colorful background with tiny unlabeled numbers

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience may not understand the evidence.

answer.text: B. A full paragraph copied from the speaker notes

feedback.text: Incorrect. Too much text weakens slide clarity.

answer.text: C. A decorative image with no evidence

feedback.text: Incorrect. Decoration does not support the claim.

answer.text: D. A labeled chart showing 68 of 120 surveyed students stay after school

feedback.text: Correct. This makes the key evidence visible and understandable.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L08_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.RS.01

Which evidence is most credible for the presentation?

answer.text: A. In a survey of 120 students, 68 reported staying on campus after school at least twice a week.

feedback.text: Correct. This is specific, measurable evidence.

answer.text: B. Some students probably want a study space.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a guess, not evidence.

answer.text: C. I think the idea sounds useful.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is an opinion without support.

answer.text: D. Everyone knows hallways are loud.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a broad claim without a source.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L08_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.V.01

Which sentence has the most appropriate tone for school leaders?

answer.text: A. This plan is awesome and people should just do it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is casual and demanding.

answer.text: B. The school better make this happen.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This tone is not respectful or academic.

answer.text: C. The proposal would provide students with a supervised academic workspace after dismissal.

feedback.text: Correct. This is formal, precise, and audience-appropriate.

answer.text: D. Lots of kids hang around, so yeah.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is casual and incomplete.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L08_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.02

What should a student check before completing the Unit 6 Assessment?

answer.text: A. Whether every slide uses a different style

feedback.text: Incorrect. Inconsistent design can distract from the message.

answer.text: B. Whether the claim, evidence, slide, speaker note, tone, and conventions work together

feedback.text: Correct. Unit 6 synthesis requires all communication parts to align.

answer.text: C. Whether the speaker note repeats the slide exactly

feedback.text: Incorrect. The note should explain evidence, not simply repeat it.

answer.text: D. Whether the presentation avoids evidence

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evidence is necessary for a supported presentation.
